description: Patch one existing sequence node in place. Call get_sequence first, select sequence.nodes[].id, inspect nodeType/config, and pass that node's updatedAt as expectedUpdatedAt. This supports every stored sequence node type, including delays, email/SMS content, actions, conditions, branches without topology changes, webhooks, and trigger settings. Delay example: changes:{ delay:{ days:7 } }. For a direct text-forward email, use changes:{ emailPreset:'minimal' } on its action_email node; this changes only that linked email's Style > Format. To restyle one email, patch changes:{ emailTheme:{ colors:{ background:'#ffffff' } } } on its action_email node - that overrides only this step's linked email and leaves the company-wide theme alone. The update is type-aware and preserves fields you omit. It cannot change nodeType, managed linked-resource IDs, or graph topology; use edit_sequence_graph for structural work. It also cannot edit the copy of an action_ab_test step: that content lives on the A/B test variants (get_sequence.sequence.emails[].abTest.variants includes the blocks), so change each one with update_ab_test_variant. If update_ab_test_variant is not in the tool list, enable it on the Sequenzy connector rather than writing through update_template. On an active sequence, set confirmLiveChange:true only after the user confirms the live behavior change. Existing recipients already waiting keep their scheduled timestamp; the new delay applies when recipients reach the node in the future.

changes.description: Type-aware patch for the existing node. Start from get_sequence.sequence.nodes[].config. For logic_delay, set exactly one of delay ({ days, hours, minutes }), delayMs, waitUntil, or waitUntilWeekday ({ day, startTime, endTime, timezone, timezoneSource, minimumWait } - hold until the next weekday window; timezoneSource 'subscriber' uses each contact's timezone; minimumWait { days, hours, minutes } waits at least that long first; waitUntilWeekday replaces the whole wait, so resend timezoneSource and minimumWait); optional label is also accepted. For action_email, use name/label, subject, previewText, html/htmlContent or blocks, emailPreset, emailTheme (per-email colors/typography/layout override - patch { colors: { background: '#ffffff' } } to repaint one step without touching the company default, or null to inherit it again), isTransactional, attachments ([{ filename, path }] URL-backed files fetched at send time; path may use {{event.*}} from the enrollment event; [] removes them), and sender/reply identity fields. For action_sms, use text, blocks, imageUrls, label, or ineligibleAction. For action_push, use title, body, url, imageUrl, iconUrl, platforms, label, ineligibleAction, or localizations (the step's versions in the workspace's other languages; the whole list is replaced, so start from the stored one; translate_push_content writes them with AI). For action_in_app, use the in-app step fields (format, title, body, buttons, style...); a custom HTML message takes format:'html' with html (the document, Braze Liquid converted) and showCloseButton. A placement item takes kind:'placement' with placement (the placement key), priority (high, medium or low) and layout (card, banner or hero). Other node types accept their editable config keys. For an existing random logic_branch, randomPercentages may be updated with one non-negative value per branch summing to 100. splitMode cannot be converted in place because condition and random splits have different graph topology; build a new random split with insert_sequence_step. Managed IDs, nodeType conversion, and branch path IDs/count are not editable here; use edit_sequence_graph for topology. Webhook header patches are merged, and redacted values from get_sequence must be omitted or replaced with a real new value. For action_email: Replacing a step's blocks keeps that step's existing Style > Format rather than the company default: a step that already had a logo or footer gets them back even if you omit them, and every block added that way is listed in the response `warnings`. Pass `emailPreset` to change the format. A step whose stored content is a single raw HTML block has no format, so replacing it with another single raw HTML block is stored exactly as sent; replacing it with native blocks converts the step and does add a footer.

emailPreset.description: For an action_email node with native Sequenzy blocks, set the linked email's per-email Style > Format. Native block emails may include supported custom HTML blocks. Use minimal for a direct text-forward note without the company logo and with the simple footer, or branded to restore branded chrome. This does not change the company-wide default. Not a lossless toggle: minimal deletes standalone logo blocks, so switching back to branded generates a new logo block with a new id and the company name as alt text - send the authored logo block in `blocks` alongside the branded update to keep it. A standalone raw HTML email does not support this field, and emailPreset must not be combined with html/htmlContent.

emailTheme.description: Visual theme override for this step's linked email only; the company-wide default is left untouched, as is every other email. Partial update: the patch merges into this email's current theme, so `{ colors: { background: '#f3f4f6' } }` repaints the outer canvas and keeps its fonts, spacing, and other colors; use colors.content for the inner card and colors.surface for nested cards. A step with no override merges into the company theme rather than the platform preset. Pass null to drop the override so the step follows the company theme again. Numeric values are clamped to supported ranges. Use update_company to change the account-wide default instead.

buttonStyle.description: How primary buttons are filled: "solid" (default) or "outline" (transparent fill with a brand-color border).

buttonText.description: Label color for solid buttons. Omit to auto-derive a readable color from the button background.

content.description: Inner content card the blocks sit on. Omit to preserve its current value; when no content color is stored, the card follows background.

layout.description: Layout settings. Every field is a number except contentAlign.

contentAlign.description: Where the content column sits in a wide email client: "center" (default) or "left" (flush left, like a plain personal email; buttons, the logo and footers move left too unless set to right, or kept centered with block `styles.keepAlign: true`). Phones show the column full width either way.

presetId.description: Theme preset to base the theme on: default, soft, editorial, or bold.

typography.description: Type settings; numbers except the font-family stacks.

footerFontFamily.description: Footer font stack, also used by the auto-added footer. null removes it.

headingFontFamily.description: Font stack for headings when it differs from the email body font. Omit so headings inherit the email font.

headingFontWeight.description: Heading weight applied to all heading levels, 300-900. Omit for the per-level defaults.

headingLetterSpacing.description: Heading letter spacing in pixels (negative = tighter), clamped to -2..4. Omit for natural tracking.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

confirmLiveChange.description: Set true only after the user explicitly confirms changing a node in an active sequence.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Required optimistic-concurrency value from get_sequence.sequence.nodes[].updatedAt. The update is rejected if that node or its linked email content changed after it was read.

name: update_sequence_node

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `update_sequence_node` MCP tool.

appUrls.description: Dashboard URLs for relevant Sequenzy resources.

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

message.description: Human-readable status, confirmation, or next-step message.

sequence.description: The sequence record returned by Sequenzy.

subscriptionUrl.description: Owner-facing subscription, upgrade, and billing-management URL when available.

url.description: Primary dashboard URL for this result.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.

warnings.description: Non-fatal cautions about content, permissions, or follow-up actions.
